name: Hashabniah
title: One of the men at the reading of the Law
summary: Hashabniah was one of the men who stood beside Ezra as he read the Law to the people in Jerusalem after their return from exile in Babylon. He is mentioned in connection with the great assembly at the Water Gate, where the people renewed their covenant with God. His role was to support and lend authority to the public reading of the Law.

keyEvents.title: The Reading of the Law at the Water Gate
keyEvents.description: Hashabniah stood at Ezra's right or left side while Ezra read the Law of Moses to all the people at the Water Gate in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: The People's Reaction to the Reading of the Law
keyEvents.description: When Ezra opened the scroll, all the people stood up. When they heard the words of the law, they wept and bowed down before the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Understanding the Law
keyEvents.description: The Levites helped the people understand the law while Ezra and his helpers, including Hashabniah, stood on the platform.

keyEvents.title: The People's Joy and Celebration
keyEvents.description: After the reading of the law, the people were encouraged to rejoice, for the joy of the Lord was their strength. This day was holy to the Lord.
